Learning & growth

Practice brings
new questions.

I am a first-year undergraduate at Central University in Moscow, studying programming, mathematics and business subjects alongside practical software development. I am interested in how a formal model helps explain a human problem—and where reality forces that model to change.

Explore the projects ↗

Questions that come from building

At T-Bank, the model was a set of experiment rules. In BPMN.space, our team worked on the transition from incomplete text to a process structure. In CODY, I explore state and context across devices. Each project gives me specific questions to take back to theory.

How I learn through projects

A small working example helps me choose a scenario, build an initial implementation, observe a failure and revise an assumption. In a team, I value explaining decisions, sharing intermediate results and acknowledging other people’s contributions. This portfolio therefore includes both personal work and shared outcomes.

What I want to explore next

I want to deepen my understanding of algorithms, distributed systems and AI evaluation: checking not only whether an output has the right format, but whether it makes sense. I am interested in environments that connect theory with projects and discussion. These projects add context to my education; formal academic records and achievements remain separate evidence.

Questions I want to explore
